title: Linearizable consensus vs Dynamo quorum vs CRDT/LWW
description: Three write-coordination classes. Overlap arithmetic, gossip merge, and a Raft majority are not interchangeable. TokenX money needs a fenced single history; ads metadata may converge.

cells.workload: Single ordered command stream: TokenX ledger mutations, lock/lease metadata, chat per-conversation seq if you put the sequencer on a Raft group. Not a high-ingest click firehose.
cells.consistency: One history. Writes commit after a current-term majority (2-of-3 in a three-replica group: leader plus either follower). Linearizable reads need ReadIndex or a bounded-clock lease plus apply wait. CAP here is partition policy: the minority cannot commit. Not a two-letter product sticker.
cells.latency: Commit RTT to a majority plus fsync. p99 includes election and serialize-on-leader. A no-op commit is not a standing license for later local reads.
cells.scaling: Vertical then shard by key into many groups. One group is one hot leader. Membership change is a protocol (joint consensus), not an autoscale replace.
cells.failure: Leader crash: new election, fencing by term/epoch. Isolated minority rejects linearizable writes. Uncommitted suffix may be overwritten. Client timeout is UNKNOWN; retry the same idempotency key. Do not auto-replay request logs.
cells.costOps: You operate quorum health, disk, and epoch fencing. Three or five failure-independent nodes per group. Cross-region consensus adds WAN RTT to every commit. Keep the log off the application hot path.
cells.whenNot: When the invariant can converge without a single order (campaign labels, presence) or when ingest needs multi-master availability more than conservation. Do not call a health-check VIP 'consensus'. Do not use etcd as the TokenX ledger at payment QPS.

cells.workload: Partition-key item access with tunable R/W. High availability writes at W=ONE: session blobs, shopping-cart documents, Ad Click campaign metadata. Query tables designed up front. Not SQL joins.
cells.consistency: Tunable W/R with W+R>N overlap under stable membership. Overlap is not linearizability. Sloppy quorums, hinted handoff, and concurrent versions need a named repair (vector or LWW). Default DynamoDB eventual reads are a different API from Cassandra QUORUM.
cells.latency: Low ms in-region when the preference list is healthy. p99 from hinted replay, read repair, hot partitions, and cross-DC ALL/LOCAL_QUORUM choice.
cells.scaling: Hash partitions / vnodes. Add nodes for write fan-out. You still own the partition key; celebrity keys throttle one vnode.
cells.failure: Node loss is expected. W=ONE versus W=ALL availability: W=ONE stays writable with one replica; W=ALL is unavailable under one loss. Unavailable also if you cannot form the named quorum. Repair and hinted handoff reconcile later. A reachable minority is not a 2-of-3 consensus majority.
cells.costOps: Compaction, repair, tombstones, and capacity alarms. Managed offerings remove JVM toil, not the model. Multi-DC multiplies repair.
cells.whenNot: Spendable TokenX balances, unique allocation that must not fork, or any object you would LWW by wall clock. Conditional writes can occupy a key; they do not make default quorum linearizable.

cells.workload: Concurrent edits that have a meaningful join: grow-only tags, observed counters, presence last-seen, Ad Click dashboard labels. Clients write without waiting for a leader.
cells.consistency: Replicas accept concurrent versions. CRDTs converge by associative, commutative, idempotent merge. LWW picks a timestamp or version tuple and discards siblings. Convergence is not business validity. Session/causal guarantees need extra metadata.
cells.latency: Local-write p50. Merge and anti-entropy add lag before readers agree. Clock skew makes LWW order an operational assumption, not physics.
cells.scaling: Any replica can take writes. Metadata (version vectors, tombstones) grows with replica/device identity unless compacted.
cells.failure: Partition is normal: both sides write. After heal, merge or LWW runs. An observed-remove set can resurrect a concurrent add. Tombstone GC too early reintroduces deletes.
cells.costOps: You test the merge under permutations and replay. You operate tombstone frontiers and identity compaction. Cheap to start; expensive when the type was wrong.
cells.whenNot: TokenX balances, reservations, or any conservation invariant. Do not LWW money, max() two replica balances, or treat a CRDT counter as a unique click_id. Security revocation usually needs monotonic-deny, not add-wins.

assumptions: Three-replica consensus majority is 2-of-3 in one region unless a cell says otherwise. Five-node groups use 3-of-5.
CAP is per-operation partition policy (TokenX debit rejects without proven authority; labeled stale reads may continue). It is not a permanent two-of-three letter choice.
Dynamo-style row means client-tunable quorum plus eventual repair, not DynamoDB ConsistentRead and not Raft.
CRDT/LWW row assumes multi-master writes with a named merge. LWW uses a clock or version tuple you must state.
Latency figures are order-of-magnitude interview planning numbers, not SLOs from a named fleet.
TokenX exclusive terminals and idempotency keys are required on money paths regardless of which class you pick; picking CRDT/LWW for balances is still wrong.
